The misbranding section requires that, for a cosmetic sold in a retail box (i.e., package form), the label must contain: (1) the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; (2) an accurate statement of the quantity of the contents in terms of weight, measure, or numerical count; and (3) the information required under section 364e of this title. This requirement applies unless exemptions are established by regulations prescribed by the Secretary for small packages, which may permit reasonable variations in the labeling. These requirements are part of what constitutes misbranding under FD&C Act § 602(b), and failure to meet them would constitute a misbranded cosmetic.

FD&C Act § 602(b) [21 U.S.C. 362(b)] requires that, for package form cosmetics, the label must contain (1) the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; (2) an accurate statement of the quantity of the contents in terms of weight, measure, or numerical count; and (3) the information required under section 364e of this title. Reasonable variations are permitted under clause (2), and exemptions for small packages may be established by regulations prescribed by the Secretary [3].
